newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends firm as money tightens.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends firm as money tightens.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed firmer at 488.25/489.25 bolivars per dollar after banks hurriedly unwound long dollar positions ahead of new commercial bank reserve requirements set to come into effect Monday, traders said.
The bolivar closed Thursday at 488.75/489.75 per dollar.

The session's volatile trade "was principally due to a shift in investors' positions ahead of the reserve requirement increase," said one trader, adding that the exchange rate should stay calm next week following the adjustment.

Banks moved into bolivars to comply with Central Bank regulations, published Thursday, that will require commercial banks to place 15 percent of their deposits in non interest- bearing Central Bank accounts.
Previously they had only had to place 12 percent.
"It (the measure) should play well as the Bank couldn't use the exchange market to soak up liquidity," said another trader.
The reserve requirement increase will dry up some of the market's recent excess liquidity that has helped push down interest rates and weaken the bolivar, traders added.
